title: Finite-evaluation primitive operator for any finite-index coset rectangle
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a profinite group $G$ (a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of open normal subgroups), an open subgroup $H\subseteq G$ of finite index $m=[G:H]$, an integer $n\geq1$, and elements $a_0,\ldots,a_n\in G$. Use $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and the universes of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], [def-weil-size-convention]. For any normed $\mathbf Q_\ell$-vector space $V$ whose norm satisfies $\|v+w\|\leq\max(\|v\|,\|w\|)$ and $\|av\|=|a|_\ell\|v\|$, put $C^r(G,V)=C(G^r,V)$ with the norm topology on $V$, trivial $G$-action, $C^0(G,V)=V$, $d^0=0$, and
$$(dc)(g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^ic(g_1,\ldots,g_i g_{i+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
There is a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear operator $T:C^n(G,V)\to C^{n-1}(G,V)$ of the form
$$(Tc)(x)=\sum_{k=1}^u\alpha_k c(\psi_k(x)),$$
where $u$ is finite, $\psi_k:G^{n-1}\to G^n$ is continuous and $\alpha_k\in\mathbf Q_\ell$ satisfies $|\alpha_k|_\ell\leq |m|_\ell^{-1}$. The choices depend only on $G,H,n,(a_i)$, not on $V$. Whenever $dc=0$ and the homogeneous function
$$f_c(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=c(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_{n-1}^{-1}g_n)$$
vanishes on $Ha_0\times\cdots\times Ha_n$, one has $d(Tc)=c$. The same formulas, leaving a profinite parameter $s\in S$ fixed, define continuous operators on $C(S\times G^n,V)$ and have supremum-norm bound $|m|_\ell^{-1}$. They preserve every $\mathbf Q_\ell$-linear coefficient subspace. No prime-to-$\ell$ condition on $m$ and no completeness of $V$ is assumed.
